summary: Preserved PR 930's DeepSeek-V4 physical-tensor memory accounting and corrected its HiSparse C4 omission by including the GPU uint64 data-pointer table in the pool's allocated tensors and mem_usage.

tests.what_was_measured: On GPU, standard FP8, FP4 and unified layouts matched owned tensor bytes; HiSparse reported 3,594,944 bytes while independently enumerated owned tensors totaled 3,594,952 bytes, an 8-byte deficit. Retained output: evidence/review_script_exact_candidate.txt.
Six tests passed with ten subtests, including one- and three-layer HiSparse pointer-table accounting boundaries.
Real gfx950 GPU allocations matched independent physical tensor byte sums for standard FP8, HIP FP4-indexer, HiSparse and unified layouts; corrected HiSparse was 3,594,952 bytes with zero delta.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) executed actual DeepSeek-V4 pool allocations; raw before/after outputs are under reports/j-21eb86c1d067/evidence/.

remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4 weights and the original 8x H100 environment were unavailable. No full HTTP-serving, CUDA, multi-rank, or model-semantic claim is made. The correction is Python-only, so no native rebuild was applicable.
